officials.bio: Arik Forsman was appointed as an At Large member of the Duluth City Council in 2018, was elected to the same post in 2019, and was re-elected in 2023. He's the former council President and 2025 chair of the Finance Committee, also serving on the Duluth Economic Development Authority and as Mayor Pro Tem from 2024-2026. Forsman has led initiatives addressing the local childcare crisis, invested in housing and public safety, and supported the TV & film industry.

She is the Owner and Principal Director of Operations for Healthy Alliances Matter LLC and Founder/Executive Director of Healthy Alliances Matter for All. She has been a Duluth resident since 1968 and has a background as a retired Physical Therapy Clinician & Director of Rehabilitation.

officials.name: David Clanaugh
officials.address: City Hall, Room 318, 411 West First Street, Duluth, MN 55802
officials.bio: Councilor David Clanaugh has been a Duluth resident for more than twenty‑six years. Raised in rural northern Wisconsin, he is an avid outdoorsman who enjoys canoeing, kayaking, hiking, skiing, gardening, and hunting. He and his wife, Tracie, have three adult children who graduated from East, Denfeld, and Harbor City schools.

officials.name: Diane Desotelle
officials.address: City Hall, Room 318, 411 West First Street, Duluth, MN 55802
officials.bio: I have lived in Duluth for 27 years where my husband and I raised two children. We are proud to say we have always lived, worked and played in this city owning one car and two bikes. Professionally, I am a civil engineer, educator, and land use planner where I worked for a variety of public and private sector entities.

officials.name: Roz Randorf
officials.address: City Hall, Room 318, 411 West First Street, Duluth, MN 55802
officials.bio: Roz Randorf is the 3rd District City Councilor for Duluth, representing precincts 14-19. She serves as 2025 Council Intergovernmental Chair, Treasurer and Commissioner for the Duluth Economic Development Authority, and a voting member of the Duluth Downtown Waterfront District. She also works as a Corporate Consultant and Certified Trainer for Dale Carnegie, North Central, US.

officials.name: Wendy Durrwachter
officials.address: City Hall, Room 318, 411 West First Street, Duluth, MN 55802
officials.bio: Wendy Durrwachter is the City Councilor for District 1, representing precincts 1-7. She serves on the Duluth Public Utilities Commission, the Duluth Public Arts Commission, and the Purchasing and Licensing Commission. Durrwachter is a composer/pianist and account manager, who grew up in Green Bay, WI and attended the U of MN Twin Cities for music.

officials.name: Mike Maguire
officials.address: Eagan Municipal Center 3830 Pilot Knob Rd. Eagan, MN 55122
officials.bio: Mike Maguire was elected Eagan's 8th Mayor in 2006, currently serving his fifth term, after previously being a City Council Member. He holds a Bachelor's from Suffolk University and a Master's from Mankato State, and has taught public speaking and communication. As Mayor, he serves on various boards and commissions, including the City Council's Finance Committee and the Eagan Convention and Visitors Bureau Board.

officials.name: Rafael E. Ortega
officials.address: 15 West Kellogg Boulevard, Room 220, Saint Paul, MN 55102
officials.bio: Commissioner Rafael E. Ortega is a progressive champion for Ramsey County, working to protect vulnerable residents, build a better transportation network, and redevelop brown fields to create jobs, housing, and increase the tax base. He grew up in poverty in New York City, received his B.A. at Fordham University, and later served as CEO of CLUES, growing the social service agency significantly. Ortega became the first person of color elected to the Ramsey County Board in 1994 and currently serves as Chair.

officials.bio: Mai Chong Xiong was elected in 2023, becoming the first Asian, first Hmong American, and youngest to serve. She is a public servant, community organizer, working mother of two young children, caregiver to elderly parents, and wife to Dan Yang. She was born and raised in Saint Paul, which her family and extended families have called home the last 35 years.

officials.name: Garrison McMurtrey
officials.address: Courthouse Room 220 15 West Kellogg Boulevard Saint Paul, MN 55102
officials.bio: Garrison McMurtrey is the first Black man elected to a county board in the state of Minnesota. Originally from Mississippi, McMurtrey moved to Minnesota to pursue a career in public policy and community engagement. Prior to being elected, McMurtrey served as the district director for the office of U.S. Congresswoman Angie Craig.

Born and raised in the Mille Lacs area, Miller has dedicated her career to public service and community advocacy. Miller resides in Maplewood with her fiancée and two children.

A lifelong Ramsey County resident now residing in Roseville, she brings a deep connection to the community she represents and a strong commitment to advancing the well‑being of her residents.

offices.name: Ramsey County Board Office

officials.bio: Rena Moran is the Ramsey County Commissioner of District 4, serving a large section of Saint Paul, including parts of Union Park, Hamline-Midway, Frogtown, Summit-University, North End, Downtown, Summit Hill, Macalester-Groveland and Highland Park. She is a former member of the Minnesota House of Representatives and the first African American to represent Saint Paul. She served six terms before retiring to run for Ramsey County Commissioner in 2022.

officials.bio: Commissioner Bethany Cox was elected to the County Board of Commissioners in November 2024 to represent District 3. Prior to her election, she served on the City of Stillwater Planning Commission and the Public Library Board of Trustees, and worked as Director of Development at the Wild Rivers Conservancy. She holds a Doctor of Chiropractic degree and lives in Stillwater with her husband and two children.

officials.name: Michelle Clasen
officials.address: P.O. Box 6 14949 62nd Street North Stillwater, MN 55082-6132
officials.bio: Michelle Clasen was elected to the District 5 seat on the Washington County Board of Commissioners in 2022. Commissioner Clasen brings more than 15 years of industry experience in public service and local government leadership, serving on boards and commissions, as well as seven years of professional experience in tort law. Her work is grounded in a commitment to practical, people-centered governance, with a focus on issues that affect residents’ daily lives—such as clean water, workforce development, mental health, climate resilience, and economic opportunity.

Now retired after a 38-year career as a principal designer at Graco, Inc., he holds nine invention patents.
